question: What is the main protein that builds human hair and nails?
explanation: Keratin is the tough, fibrous protein that forms the core structure of your hair, nails, and the outer layer of your skin. Great job knowing this basic building block! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the main job of the sebum (oil) secreted by scalp glands?
explanation: Sebum is a natural oil that keeps your scalp and hair from drying out. Think of it as your body's built-in moisturizer! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h1)

question: When checking a patient's scalp, what sign is a dead giveaway for head lice?
explanation: Nits are tiny, oval eggs laid by head lice. They stick tightly to individual hairs near the scalp, making them easy to spot once you know what to look for. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: A patient has sudden patches of hair loss and a scaly scalp. What should you suspect?
explanation: Patchy hair loss with scaling often points to ringworm of the scalp (tinea capitis), a common fungal infection that needs proper treatment. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which part of your hand should you use to massage a patient's scalp during a bed shampoo?
explanation: Always use the pads of your fingers! Using fingernails can scratch and hurt the patient's sensitive scalp. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why must you always check the water temperature before washing a bedridden patient's hair?

options.A: To ensure the soap lathers properly
options.B: To avoid shocking the hair roots
options.C: To prevent thermal burns on the scalp
options.D: To keep the patient from feeling cold

explanation: Some patients might not be able to tell if water is too hot. Checking it yourself keeps them safe from accidental burns. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why are tightly coiled or curly hair types usually drier than straight hair?

options.A: The scalp produces significantly less sebum
options.B: The hair shaft lacks an outer cuticle layer
options.C: Natural oils travel less easily down the shaft
options.D: Frequent washing strips out moisture quickly

explanation: Because of the bends and curves in curly hair, it's harder for natural scalp oils to slide all the way down to the ends. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the safest way to detangle long hair for a patient who is on bed rest?

options.A: Pulling firmly from the scalp down to the tips
options.B: Using a fine-toothed comb on dry hair all at once
options.C: Gently working from the hair ends up to the roots
options.D: Cutting out any small knots to save time

explanation: Always start at the ends and work your way up! This avoids painful pulling and keeps the hair from breaking. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the medical name for a head lice infestation?
explanation: Pediculosis capitis is the clinical term you'll see in charts for head lice. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT part of treating head lice?

options.A: Washing bed linens in hot water
options.B: Combing out nits with a fine-toothed comb
options.C: Applying antibiotic ointment to the scalp

explanation: Lice are tiny bugs (parasites), not bacteria. Antibiotics won't help here—we use medicated shampoos and fine-toothed combs instead! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h5)

question: When charting a patient's hair and scalp care, what kind of details should you write down?
explanation: Good nursing documentation sticks to the facts: what you actually saw, and how the patient handled the care procedure. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: A patient asks how often they should wash their hair. What is the best nursing reply?

options.A: Every single day without fail to prevent bacterial buildup
options.B: Only when visible dirt and odor begin to appear
options.C: Frequency depends on hair type, activity level, and personal needs
options.D: Once a month to preserve all natural scalp oils

explanation: There is no single rule! Hair washing depends on texture, oiliness, lifestyle, and personal preference. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)
